name: Shrimp With Chorizo-Tomato Sauce

ingredients.name: chipotle chilis, canned in adobo sauce
unsalted butter, cut into four pieces

instructions.primary_message: In a medium bowl, toss shrimp, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and pepper to combine; set aside.

In a 30-cm stainless steel skillet, heat 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add chorizo, onion, and remaining 3 smashed garlic cloves, and cook until onion is softened and beginning to brown, 4 to 5 minutes. Add tomatoes, chipotle in adobo, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and cook until tomato begins to break down and a browned layer begins to form on the bottom of the pot, 3 to 4 minutes.

Add wine and cook until reduced by half, scraping up the browned bits on bottom of skillet, about 2 minutes. Add chicken stock or broth. Increase heat to medium-high and bring to a vigorous simmer. Simmer until reduced by half (about 2 1/4 cups), 10 to 12 minutes.
Carefully transfer chorizo mixture to a blender and process on high until smooth, 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down sides of blender jar as needed. Rinse and dry the skillet.

Return now-clean skillet to medium-high heat and heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil in skillet until just smoking. Add shrimp and cook, stirring occasionally, until shrimp are opaque and just cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes.

Add sauce and bring to a simmer, about 30 seconds. Off heat, stir in butter and lemon juice until butter is melted. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with crusty bread.

schema_metadata.keywords: Shrimp With Chorizo-Tomato Sauce, shrimp recipe, shrimp and chorizo recipe

description: This easy shrimp dinner features a smoky Spanish chorizo sauce blended with tomatoes, garlic, chipotles, and white wine for bold flavor in about 30 minutes.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Crusty bread, for serving

Optional substitutions: dry white wine → dry sherry; homemade chicken stock → store-bought low-sodium chicken broth

Notes: While fish counters often sell shrimp as “medium” or “large,” the industry usually sizes them by count per pound. For this recipe, shrimp in the 21/25 or 26/30 range—roughly medium to medium-large—work well.
Sherry can be substituted for white wine to add a more oaky, nutty flavor, if desired.
1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper can be substituted for chipotle in adobo.

Make-ahead and storage: The sauce can be made up to 2 days ahead. To finish, season the shrimp and let sit for 15 to 20 minutes. Meanwhile, rewarm the sauce in a small saucepan, then continue to step 5.
author: Amanda Luchtel
